steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x5 inch loaf pan.

Mix the beef, pork, egg, apple, onion, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper in a mixing bowl until evenly mixed. Add the Cheddar cheese, bread crumbs, and oats; mix again until evenly mixed. Pack the meat mixture into the prepared loaf pan.

Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, about 1 hour. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (72 degrees C). Allow the meatloaf to rest for 10 minutes before slicing to keep the meat from crumbling.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Apple and Oat Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: Minced apple and Cheddar cheese set this meatloaf apart from the rest.

review.reviewBody: excellent. i made a few adjustments based on what i had on hand - (1) swapped out the oats for 1/4 cup of flax seed and (2) went with 3/4 lb of ground beef + 3/4 pound of ground turkey (no pork). perfect, will have the leftovers tonight and definitely make it again.

I did make a couple of changes, but it was still the same recipe and the apple was terrific. I just plain forgot the cheddar cheese. Used one whole apple (McIntosh), minced, didn't measure. Added one stalk minced celery, and reduced the onion a bit. Reduced the Worcestershire. Used 2 eggs. It was very good and moist and the little bit of sweetness and tang from the apple was wonderful. I served it with homemade mushroom gravy and mashed potatoes. Thank you for the recipe. To those who say there was no apple flavor, I wonder what variety of apple you were using. Or, perhaps were you eating it with ketchup, which would cover up the appleness. I normally put ketchup on meatloaf, but would not put ketchup on this one.

This is very good. We're always looking for new ideas for apples in the fall. I used venison instead of beef/pork and it still came out great. I also added thin slices of apples on top of the meatloaf that were basted with worcester - definitely a good decision. 4-year old cheddar added a sharper flavor to the meatloaf and was very good. Next time I would add an extra layer of cheese on top and perhaps more apples in the loaf.

Love this recipe. Made it exactly following recipe (other than doubling the recipe and shaping into 3 loafs in a large pan in order to freeze and save two) and I enjoyed it but hubby thought it had a little too much filler (bread crumbs). Now I modify it just a bit: ground turkey, a scant quarter cup of wheat germ to replace the 1/2 cup of bread crumbs, a little extra apple, and it's perfect for our whole family!

My husband, a basic palate-preferences meat and potatoes guy, was just diagnosed with diabetes. I’ve been working hard to find recipes he will like and meet his carb limitations. I subbed turkey for the pork due to using what I have and couldn’t be happier with how it turned out. A delicious, flavorful spin on a classic. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
I didn't have beef, so I used only pork and used apple cinnamon oats that my son never ate. It was a hit and I am making it again this evening. I love that it is so open to interpretation.
Great Meatloaf, used ground venison from a white tail, and some left over ground pork trimmings, 3/4C of diced apple and an extra sharp cheddar. Plenty moist yet did not crumble too bad.

I'm on a health kick so I made a couple edits. I replaced the beef with ground turkey and added applesauce for moisture. I left out the salt but added steak seasoning. It held together well and my family really enjoyed it. I will make it again.

I was never a big fan of meatloaf but my husband always was. His mother used to make an apple meatloaf so I decided to look up recipes. When I came across this I decided to give it a try using just beef. I loved it but made a few adjustments the next time I made it, doubling the apple and tomato paste instead of worcestershire. But definitely a great recipe!!!

This recipe was unbelievable--my husband went back for seconds and asked for leftovers! I tweaked a bit as I did not have any ground pork. To compensate I just lessened the other ingredients slightly and made a smaller loaf with the 1 lb of ground beef only. I also spread a simple topping of 1/4 c. ketchup plus 1T. mustard before baking. Simply superb!

A dense and hearty, stick to your ribs meatloaf with a hint of cheese. Used one packet of instant oatmeal (which is just shy of a 1/2 cup), and two Italian sausages (casings removed), omitted salt & pepper. Baked for one hour at 350 degrees.
Delicious

Pretty good, but mine needed more salt. I'm also not sure if my thermometers weren't working or not but mine seemed too dry at the recommended internal temperature. I didn't have any ground pork, like I thought I did so I also did all beef so that probably made a difference too. I'd try this again with the pork.

Yes, I would definitely make it again...I did add some garlic powder to the meat mixture and can't make any meatloaf without adding the catsup/brown sugar mixture for the top of the loaf...no bacon, just catsup and brown sugar. This was definitely a keeper.
Really good recipe.
Easy to make and tastes very nice
this was so delicious!! moist and tasty my 4 yr old helps me cook and bake and she loved it so much she ate a large slice!!!

Very tasty. Love the apples in with the meat! I did add a little more apples to the meat. I also used Italian bread crumbs and add about a clove of garlic. Super yummy! Will definitely be making this one again.
Very, very good recipe. Great combination of flavors. I didn't change anything at all, and it turned out fantastic. Very moist, flavorful and simple. Even my picky inlaws liked this.
2 out of 4 tasters thought it was ok, so I won't be repeating this one.
